volume.source: Aalborg Portland, White Concrete Technology, p4: absolute cement density 3150 kg/m3; https://www.aalborgportland.com.my/wp-content/uploads/info_white_concrete_technology.pdf
volume.role: Additive initial constituent volumes with the cement product density and water density at 20 C. Dunant et al. vibrated the specimens to remove air; fresh density and air fraction were not measured for these batches.

thermal_properties.source: Bentz (2007), doi:10.1617/s11527-006-9206-9, sections 3.1-3.2, Eq (1)-(2), Fig 4; full text https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225639675_Transient_plane_source_measurements_of_the_thermal_properties_of_hydrating_cement_pastes
thermal_properties.role: Mixture heat capacity uses fresh constituent values; conductivity is a nominal Portland-cement-paste estimate. These are assumed thermal properties, not measurements on the W32/W40/W48 batches.

temperature_response.source: Granja et al. (2023), doi:10.3151/jact.21.803, Table 6: paste early-stage values 37.32-39.58 kJ/mol. This separate CEM I w/c=0.54 experiment supplies the nominal scale, not W32/W40/W48 calibration.
temperature_response.role: Prescribed Arrhenius rate scaling; the selected model domain ends at 40 C or the end of the measured heat-state map.

boundaries.role: Reservoir exchange at the lining intrados and paste/soil interface. The prescribed initial and reservoir temperatures are 20 C.

initial_state: The common observation age 1.68637216 h supplies the measured nonzero stiffness and q=0 observed heat increment. The construction clock starts at this state; mechanical activation does not reset it.
